chapter: Small groups, Europe and Kansas City memories (repeated passages)
title: Why rehearsals can be boring
summary: Morgenstern tells how Lester left Basie out of boredom with rehearsals; Dickenson has players learn parts at home first.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Lester once said that he left Basie eventually because he got bored running through things all the time, and like rehearsing things that he already knew.
He said it's just like when he was in school, and he'd learned his lessons and the other kids hadn't, and so he'd
go to sleep because he knew them, and then the teacher would wake him up and tell his parents that he was snoring in class.
Oh, they can get boring, all right, them rehearsals.. They usually get...
But I guess it's necessary, though, if you want to have a...

Well, I don't know... I guess it is. It is necessary to learn it, all right. But you know, I would let the guys take the music home first, and run over it by themselves, or get one of the guys that knows it, and get a bottle, and have a ball, and learn it like that. Learn it just with the other guy, you know. You don't have them all doing it. Just get the one that knows it all right, and make him happy while you're playing, while you're doing it. You know, you all do it together just...
[He skinned him. How do you like that? He skunked him! Ha-ha... Oh boy. Well, that shows you. Yanks gotta wake up this next ballgame.]
